issues.legal_issue: A local authority cannot condition approval of a land layout plan on the owner transferring land reserved for public use to the authority free of cost when no law authorizes that transfer.
material_facts: The owner submitted a layout plan reserving land for a park, school and other public purposes.
The authority approved building activity subject to the condition that the open spaces for parks and schools be transferred to it free of cost.
The applicable legislation allowed conditions on layout-plan approval but contained no provision vesting such reserved land in the authority or requiring its free transfer.
issues.conclusion: The authority was not entitled to require free transfer of ownership. Reserving land for public use may limit the owner’s ability to use or dispose of it and may give the authority a right to manage it, but does not itself vest ownership in the authority.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 312 and 313 of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, the authority may require particulars and impose conditions serving the purpose of layout-plan regulation, including reservation of sites for public purposes. That power does not authorize requiring the owner to surrender land free of cost. The Act’s provisions dealing with private streets do not provide for parks or school sites to vest in the authority; even a private street becomes public only through the statutory process. Reservation for public use is distinct from transfer of ownership, although it may create a trust-like obligation and permit management in the public interest. D.L.E. Housing & Construction (P) Ltd. v. Delhi Municipal Corporation was distinguished because it construed a separate regulation that expressly required free transfer. The Court also observed that the absence of authority to transfer the property could not be supplied by the former statutory regime considered in that case.

predicates.layout_plan_approval_proceeding: An authority is considering or has granted approval for a land layout plan.
predicates.free_transfer_condition: The authority makes approval conditional on the owner transferring reserved land to it without payment.
predicates.no_law_authorizes_transfer: No applicable law authorizes the authority to obtain ownership of the reserved land by requiring its free transfer.

issues.definition: When approval of a land layout plan is conditioned on free transfer and no law authorizes that transfer, the condition is unlawful.

issues.legal_issue: An unlawful free-transfer condition need not result in the existing arrangement being set aside where doing so would disrupt a long-settled situation, provided the authority’s role and the land’s public use are protected.
material_facts: The owner did not object immediately to the condition and proceeded to sell and transfer land in the colony.
The owner filed suit after a delay, and the authority had exercised rights over the land for nearly a quarter of a century.
The Court considered that undoing the arrangement would unsettle the existing situation and sought to protect the interests of the colony’s owners and residents.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not set aside the lower courts’ orders, but modified the arrangement: the authority could manage the land reserved for public purposes, could not change its use from benefiting the colony’s residents, and could obtain transfer of the land by paying its market price as at the time the layout plan was approved.
issues.legal_principle: The Court may tailor relief to do substantial justice rather than undo a long-established arrangement, while protecting affected residents. Management of reserved land does not amount to ownership; the authority’s management must preserve the land’s designated beneficial use. Transfer to the authority remains possible on payment of the specified market price. The Court relied on the facts that the owner had not objected promptly, had proceeded to deal with the land, and the authority had exercised rights over it for a substantial period.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_land_transfer_arrangement and owner_delayed_objection and owner_dealt_with_land and authority_long_exercised_rights

predicates.appeal_challenging_land_transfer_arrange: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an existing arrangement concerning land reserved for public use.
predicates.owner_delayed_objection: The owner did not object promptly to the condition affecting the reserved land.
predicates.owner_dealt_with_land: The owner proceeded to sell or otherwise transfer land after the condition was imposed.
predicates.authority_long_exercised_rights: The authority exercised rights over the reserved land for a substantial period before the dispute was finally considered.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a land-transfer arrangement after delayed objection, dealings with the land, and the authority’s long exercise of rights, the arrangement may be preserved subject to limits on management, use, and transfer.
